key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than trap light: they also improve film wetting, crystal quality, charge extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texturing is a multi-functional design strategy that can boost photovoltaic performance and device durability, making it valuable for perovskite solar cells and related optoelectronic devices.
method: Review of recently reported texture-related benefits beyond light management
Focus on wetting, crystallinity, carrier extraction, and mechanical stability
Connects texture design to both performance and reliability improvements
evidence_signal: The paper synthesizes recent reported studies rather than presenting new experimental data, highlighting recurring improvements in wetting, crystal morphology, open-circuit voltage, and flexibility-related stability.
watch_item: Texture benefits may depend strongly on texture geometry, fabrication compatibility, and perovskite processing conditions, so gains may not transfer universally across device stacks.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
